expectation: Cytoplasmic or fibrous filaments in mesenchymal cells: stromal fibroblasts, vessel endothelium, smooth muscle, plus immune cells. Common in stroma, lamina propria and muscle wall; epithelium should be negative.
observed: A: strong in the stroma and muscle wall, with fibrous streaks; epithelial villi/glands are dark blue. B and C: epithelial bands are negative, with scattered small positive cells in and near them, and a bright stromal patch. D: cytoplasmic rings around dark nuclei, with spindle cells.
why: VIM lights the stroma and mesenchymal compartment and spares the epithelium, in a cytoplasmic pattern around nuclei, which is what a working mesenchymal marker looks like.
notes: VIM fills the stroma and muscle wall and leaves the epithelial glands and villi dark. At cell scale it sits in the cytoplasm around the nuclei of spindle and scattered cells. This is clear, specific structure.
